item.title: US aircraft evacuated from second British base due to Iran threat, WSJ reports
item.description:
Nov 10 (Reuters) - The US military evacuated aircraft from a second airbase in Britain on Monday after a threat from Iran, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter, weeks after Washington withdrew its bombers from RAF Fairford airbase over asuspected Iran-linked security incident.

Two USrefueling tankers that were using the RAF Mildenhall military base diverted to Germany earlier on Monday, while several other tankers at the base were moved to Germany and other locations later in the day, the WSJ report said.

item.title: Saudi-led coalition reports Houthi missile, drone interceptions; Saba reports Saudi strikes on Sanaa
item.description: Nov 10 (Reuters) - The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Tuesday it intercepted two missiles launched by Yemen's Iran-alignedHouthis towards Riyadh, a ballistic missile fired towards the kingdom's southern region and a drone over its oil-rich Eastern Province, in a night of heightened military activity across Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Saudi official inspects Aramco Riyadh office after Houthi attack
item.description:
Nov 10 (Reuters) - Saudi Arabia's deputy governor of Riyadh inspected an Aramco administrative building in the capital that was damaged in an attack by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group, state news agency SPA reported early on Tuesday.

Prince Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Abdulaziz said the attack underscored theHouthis' targeting of civilian facilities, SPA said. He directed authorities to provide support for Aramco employees.

item.title: US-mediated talks with Russia and Ukraine to start in Abu Dhabi
item.description:
Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States will hold talks in Abu Dhabi Tuesday on ending Europe's worst conflict since World War II, in the first such meeting in more than nine months.

Europe -- alarmed by US President Donald Trump floating a deal with Moscow on European security ahead of the talks -- will also send representatives to Abu Dhabi, as another winter of war approaches.

item.title: How Israel's new parliament can make Netanyahu's life difficult
item.description:
Benjamin Netanyahu remains Israel's prime minister when the new parliament takes office Tuesday but its new, less friendly composition could make his life much more difficult.

Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief seeking to move Israel to the centre, was given the mandate Sunday by President Isaac Herzog to form a new government, a complicated task as neither he nor Netanyahu command a majority.

item.title: Russia, Ukraine to meet for US-backed talks after Trump says broad deal possible
item.description:
By Daniel Flynn and Steve Holland

KYIV/WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - Russian and Ukrainian officials planned to meet on Tuesday for two days of US-brokered talks — their first since February — after President Donald Trump suggested last week that a broad peace deal was possible in their 4-1/2-year-old war and could incorporate Europe's security.

European powers, including France, Germany and the European Commission, will send officials to the talks in Abu Dhabi, but Russia has made it clear it doesn’t want the Europeans to take part in negotiations.

item.title: Trump sees 'positive momentum' on Iran after Qatar PM talks
item.description:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday there was momentum toward ending the war with Iran, as he declared that the country "militarily, is effectively over," but kept open the possibility of new strikes.

Trump met at the White House with Qatar Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani -- a key mediator in the Iran war. It was his first meeting with a foreign leader since his party's massive losses in the midterm elections.

item.title: Zelenskiy says Ukrainian battlefield successes strengthen Kyiv's position in talks
item.description:
Nov 9 (Reuters) - President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, on the eve of US-led, three-sided talks on resolving the war with Russia, that Ukrainian battlefield successes and mounting Russian losses were strengthening Kyiv's position in negotiations.

The talks with Russian and US negotiators, opening on Tuesday in Abu Dhabi, will be the first since February aimed at bringing closer an end to the more than 4-1/2-year-old war.

"Ukrainian forces are currently genuinely strengthening Ukraine's negotiating position," Zelenskiy said in his nightly video address.

item.title: Trump says US military action against Iran not necessary 'at this point'
item.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 9 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump on Monday told reporters that military action by the United States against Iran did not currently seem necessary.

"At this point ... taking the military action doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing. But we're locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes," Trump told reporters.

"I think it's going to be ending fairly soon," he said, referring to the conflict against Tehran.

(Reporting by Steve Holland, writing by Bhargav Acharya;Editing by David Ljunggren)

item.title: Trump tells Reuters that Qatar, Saudi Arabia want peaceful Iran deal, US ready for strikes if needed
item.description:
By Steve Holland

WASHINGTON, Nov 9 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump told Reuters on Monday that Qatar and Saudi Arabia were eager for a peaceful solution on the Iran conflict but the United States was ready to resume military strikes if necessary.

Trump, who met Qatar's prime minister earlier on Monday, said "Qatar would rather see a peaceful solution" and "Saudi Arabia would rather see a peaceful solution" but "we're ready to go anytime we want" with strikes.

item.title: Merz says Germany faces historic test over rise in antisemitism
item.description:
BERLIN, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Monday that Germany faced a test of its commitment to protecting its Jewish community as he decried the "horrifying sight" of kindergartens and synagogues protected by bulletproof glass and armed police.

Speaking at a Munich synagogue on the anniversary of the "Kristallnacht" pogrom in 1938, which foreshadowed the Nazi Holocaust that would eventually slaughter more than 6 million European Jews, Merz said antisemitism had become "omnipresent".

item.title: Trump 'Board of Peace' says Israel too slow as floods ravage Gaza
item.description:
President Donald Trump's "Board of Peace" said Monday that Israel needed to act immediately to help war-battered Gaza cope with impending winter, saying measures ahead of deadly floods had been insufficient.

"The situation no longer represents simply a threat posed by the approaching winter, but an immediate humanitarian emergency," the Board of Peace said in a statement.

item.title: To unseat Netanyahu, Israel's once-unyielding Liberman turns to compromise
item.description:
He built his career on unyielding principles, but the Israeli secular nationalist Avigdor Liberman is now preaching compromise in a bid to bring down Benjamin Netanyahu, his former mentor whom he now despises.

For three decades, Liberman's steely blue eyes, steadily greying whiskers and ample use of chess metaphors have been an ever-present part of Israeli political life.

So too has been the unwavering defence of secularism by the 68-year-old immigrant from the former Soviet Union, as religious Jews gain political influence inside Israel.

item.title: Syria denies sending troops to fight Houthis in return for Saudi loans
item.description: The Saudi Fund for Development and Syria’s Finance Ministry recently inked more than $403 million in concessional loan agreements, fueling speculation that Damascus agreed to provide military support to Saudi Arabia in exchange for financial aid.

item.title: Slotkin, Van Hollen emerge as potential challengers to Schumer’s Senate leadership
item.description: A growing number of Democrats are calling for new leadership in the Senate to replace Schumer, arguing that the party needs a leader who better reflects its generational and ideological shift to the left.

item.title: Steel plant blast kills 16 in western Turkey
item.description:
ANKARA, Nov 9 (Reuters) - A blast at a steel and iron manufacturing plant in western Turkey on Monday killed 16 people, President Tayyip Erdogan said after a cabinet meeting.

• An explosion took place at around noon (0900 GMT) at the Habas iron and steel manufacturing plant in the Aliaga district of the coastal Izmir province, the governor's office said in a statement

• According to initial findings, the incident occurred when a ceiling crane snapped and fell into an arc furnace during the liquid steel casting process

item.title: France launches G7+ ports alliance to target global narcotics routes
item.description:
PARIS, Nov 9 (Reuters) - France said on Monday it had launched a new G7-backed network linking major ports, customs services and international organisations in an effort to improve intelligence sharing and coordination against global drug trafficking routes.

• France formally launched the initiative during a meeting of foreign ministers from the Group of Seven (Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States) in Paris on November 9 to 10.
